# configloader

A tiny loader for `.ini`-style config with typed values.

## Specification

Implement two functions in `configloader/loader.py`:

### `parse_config(text: str) -> dict`

Parse config text into a nested dict `{section: {key: value}}`.

- Lines are `key = value`. Leading/trailing whitespace is stripped from both.
- `[section]` lines open a section. Keys before any section go in `""` (the empty-string section).
- Blank lines and lines starting with `#` or `;` are ignored (comments).
- Values are coerced: `true`/`false` (case-insensitive) to bool, integers to int, floats to float, everything else stays a string. Quoted values (`"..."`) keep their inner text as a string, always.

### `get(config: dict, dotted: str, default=None)`

Look up `"section.key"` in a parsed config; return `default` if absent. A dotted key with no section (`"key"`) looks in the `""` section.

from configloader import parse_config, get


def test_sections_and_types():
    text = """
# a comment
mode = fast
[server]
port = 8080
ratio = 0.5
debug = TRUE
name = "prod-01"
"""
    cfg = parse_config(text)
    assert cfg[""]["mode"] == "fast"
    assert cfg["server"]["port"] == 8080
    assert cfg["server"]["ratio"] == 0.5
    assert cfg["server"]["debug"] is True
    assert cfg["server"]["name"] == "prod-01"


def test_get_dotted():
    cfg = parse_config("[db]\nhost = local\ntimeout = 30\n")
    assert get(cfg, "db.host") == "local"
    assert get(cfg, "db.timeout") == 30
    assert get(cfg, "db.missing", "x") == "x"
    assert get(cfg, "nope.nope") is None


def test_quoted_numbers_stay_strings():
    cfg = parse_config('v = "12"\n')
    assert get(cfg, "v") == "12"

I implemented `parse_config` and `get` in `configloader/loader.py` per the spec in `README.md`.

- `parse_config(text)` walks the text line by line: it strips whitespace, skips blank lines and `#`/`;` comments, opens sections on `[section]` lines (keys before any section go under `""`), and splits `key = value` on the first `=`. Values are coerced by a helper: double-quoted values keep their inner text as a string; otherwise `true`/`false` (case-insensitive) become bools, then integer parsing is tried, then float, falling back to the raw string.
- `get(config, dotted, default=None)` splits the dotted key on the last `.` (so a bare `"key"` looks in the `""` section) and returns the value or `default` if the section or key is missing.

All three tests in `tests/test_loader.py` pass via `python3 -m pytest -q`.
